doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

title: Profanity on Sun Ra's 'Nuclear War'
summary: Asked about the profanity on 'Nuclear War', Gordon says a changed band was keeping up with the times.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: I’ve got to ask you, Sun Ra is well known for having had certain moral standards and standards of behavior and not liking drugs and alcohol, things like that. And I can think of one Sun Ra record where there’s a very prominent profanity in the song “Nuclear War.”
Was that one that possibly Danny Ray Thompson was talking about? Because you didn’t hear that word the M-F word on commercial recordings too much in the early 80s.

Yeah, well you know all things change in time you know. That was a different band than — you know these guys like a lot of them had passed away and the band turned over, and things changed. So you know that record really was keeping up with current trends. Okay? It’s not like Sun Ra was a I don’t know a pilgrim or some kind of you know, got offended by things so I would say that it was really just part of keeping up with the times, Christian. Yeah.
